headers.comment: Cache busting: run `tool/web_cache_bust.sh` after every Flutter web build. It appends ?v=<content-hash> to stable Flutter entrypoint URLs, deferred JS parts, the PDF render worker, and bundled fonts. Those content-addressed URLs can be cached for a year, while the bootstrap/manifests/root documents below are always revalidated so the next page load discovers the new hashes.

Cross-origin isolation: enables SharedArrayBuffer, which skwasm's multithreaded renderer uses (without it, --wasm falls back to single-threaded skwasm_heavy) and which lets the in-browser OCR (ocr_web.dart, onnxruntime-web) run multithreaded. COEP is `credentialless`, not `require-corp`: both isolate the page (crossOriginIsolated === true on Chromium/Firefox), but `require-corp` ALSO demands every cross-origin subresource send a CORP header, and the OCR loads onnxruntime-web's script and WASM from jsDelivr, which doesn't. `credentialless` loads cross-origin resources without credentials instead of requiring CORP, so that fetch works while the page keeps its isolation. The OCR models themselves are same-origin (ocr/pp-ocrv5-mobile/, put in the build by tool/fetch_ocr_models.sh). Safari has no credentialless support, so it just isn't cross-origin isolated there (single-threaded skwasm_heavy + single-threaded OCR) - an acceptable fallback. The Flutter shell + skwasm assets are same-origin; PDFs come from the local file picker (not fetched).
